His work at Erigon focused on prototyping features and squeezing more speed out of the protocol without changing it through hard forks. events.excerpt: How do you think you're going to die? If you go by the current statistics for deaths in the US , it's reasonable to expect that cancer or heart disease will eventually get you. But OpenAI Foundation board member and Alignment Research Center Executive Director Paul Cristiano thinks we should all be worried about another major mortality risk. Speaking at a lecture series this week , Cristiano bluntly told the audience in a Toronto Convention Center, "I think for most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident." In the opening lecture of a three-part series , Cristiano outlined his worries about the risk of an impending "AI takeover." He defined that as a situation where goal-pursuing AI systems "call the shots in the same sense that humans today call the shots and what happens on Earth" and where any human trying to stop them "would be as ineffective as if you or me was trying to stop the US military." Such a situation would likely lead to mass death and perhaps uninhabitable environments for humans, Cristiano said. Read full article Comments
events.headline: OpenAI board member worries an AI "takeover" of society could be months away

events.excerpt: Kraken’s parent company, Payward, earned much less in the third quarter because fewer people traded crypto, according to the company’s financial results for the third quarter of 2026. The falling price of bitcoin is also hurting Payward’s loans. The company has not listed its shares on the stock market yet, and it is trying to prove it can earn through a down cycle. Why is Payward earning less? Kraken’s parent company, Payward, makes most of its money from fees when people buy and sell crypto. It also lends money to other crypto companies. However, falling crypto prices are hurting both parts of its business. With less people trading due to price drops, Payward is collecting fewer fees. The bitcoin that borrowers put up as security for their loans has also lost value, which makes those loans riskier. The company’s third-quarter numbers already show the drop in fees. According to a letter sent to shareholders, Payward’s adjusted EBITDA was $60 million, down 67% from a year earlier. The total value of trades on the platform fell 30% to $353 billion. Its platform margin, which it now reports instead of adjusted revenue, fell 12% to $487 million. However, the number of accounts holding any money rose by 37% to 7.1 million. The quarter was also better than the one before it. Adjusted
events.headline: Crypto downturn hits Kraken twice, as exchange and as lender

events.excerpt: The AI Compute Race report prices GPU compute outside the biggest buyers: a three-year commitment cuts the median price by 48%, while 17 of 22 tracked GPU models rose in price over the past year DALLAS, Texas – November 13, 2026 – Fluence has published The AI Compute Race , a report that prices GPU cloud compute for every company that is not a frontier lab or a hyperscaler. It was produced with research partners NEAR AI , io.net , Boundless , Phala , Gensyn , Fortytwo , Theta , Compute Labs and GAIB . Its central finding: where a company buys a GPU-hour sets the price. Across H100, H200 and B200 models, hyperscalers list GPUs at 1.98 times the GPU-cloud median, from 1.4 times on the B200 to 2.8 times on the H100. The same H200 lists from $4.08 to $10.60 an hour. Commitment length matters almost as much as provider choice. Against each provider’s own on-demand rate, a one-year reservation cuts the median price by 21% and a three-year term by 48%. Spot capacity lists at 53% of on-demand, for workloads that can be interrupted. Buyers who expect GPU prices to fall may need to recheck their budgets. Seventeen of the 22 GPU models tracked by GetDeploying cost more than a year earlier, and the median H100 rents for 13% to 30% more, depending on the window measured. The report also trace
events.headline: Hyperscalers List GPUs at Nearly 2× the GPU-Cloud Price, Fluence Research Finds

events.excerpt: A South Korean court has jailed a money launderer for two and a half years in a fake-coin investment scam, using a new crypto protection law for fraud. Prosecutors are now using the Virtual Asset User Protection Act against ordinary scams, even without a referral from regulators. What did the court decide in the fake-coin scam case? A court in Goyang found that a ring ran a fake investment website and sold tokens that did not exist. The scammers told buyers the tokens were cheap and would pay off once they were listed on an exchange even though they never planned to give buyers anything. The man who laundered the money, known only as “A,” was sentenced to two and a half years in prison. “A” became a registered gift-certificate dealer, giving the scammers a bank account to receive the money in. From late December 2024 to February 2025, fourteen victims sent him about 501 million won (roughly $345,000) in 76 transfers. After he received the money, he would send it along to the “higher ups” as cash or vouchers, earning up to 150,000 to 200,000 won a day (roughly $103 to $138) for his efforts. events.excerpt: Solo, Mozilla's LLM-powered website builder and hosting service, is shutting down. All sites and data will be deleted on November 30. Mozilla launched Solo in December 2023 as a "Mozilla Innovation Project," aimed at helping sole traders to build themselves a webpage for their services. S ome 54,000 people used its LLM to build pages, and relied on Mozilla to host them – complete with custom domain names. Well, not any more. Now the Soloist.ai homepage says: "We've made the difficult decision to close Solo. We have appreciated all of your support building and growing this product, and the feedback we've received from all of you. Solo will cease operations on Nov 30, 2026." Users now have just over two weeks left to find a new home for their pages, although Mozilla says it first notified them on October 1. According to the support FAQ , users can download a ZIP containing an HTML export, contact form and newsletter submissions, and a CSV linking to their images. The images themselves must be downloaded separately. Domains purchased through Solo Domains must also be moved to Name.com , with Mozilla handling the transfer after users create an account and supply its code. So much for having the fiddly bits taken care of. It also points at a couple of other bot-based site-generating s

events.excerpt: Two email addresses used to send bomb threats that disrupted thousands of Italian schools this week were found exposed in infostealer logs for over a year, experts say. Researchers at Hudson Rock looked into the two university email addresses used to send the bomb threats. One, from Egypt’s Kafrelsheikh University, was scooped up by Vidar – a cybercrime tool that steals saved account credentials and passwords from an infected computer and leaks them to attackers – as far back as October 2021. The other, from Taiwan's Dayeh University, was found among the 284 million addresses included in the massive AlienTXTBASE infostealer dump , dated February 2025. The experts said that the two addresses in infostealer logs do not strictly mean that those behind the bomb threats gained access to the accounts using the previous infostealer compromise. However, it suggests that there was ample time for the universities and Microsoft, which both universities used for authentication, to take action against the accounts that they should have been aware were appearing in infostealer logs. Modern threat intelligence has made infostealer logs highly visible. "Both findings place credential exposure well before the disruption, creating a substantial window in which exposed access could have been invest
events.headline: Email addresses used in European school bomb hoaxes spotted in old infostealer logs

events.excerpt: Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day. On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System , which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System. Turning a Windows defense against itself The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions. The exploit uses Windows Defender to open a log file created by a standard user by calling ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature, a legitimate Defender function for processing antivirus signature updates. Read full article Comments
events.headline: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights

Reuters reported that the project aims to keep people shopping on Amazon instead of using AI tools to find and buy products. Data on every item, whether Amazon sells it or not The idea is to give shoppers all the information they need on Amazon. They could compare products, check which vacuum cleaner is the newest, or find a tablet that meets their needs without visiting other websites. The plan appears in a roughly six-page document where it describes the new ideas and explains why they are worth developing. The document lists October 1, 2027, as a potential launch date. events.excerpt: Solo’s SDK confirms that each JellyJelly account belongs to a real, unique person, after a Solo AI agent passed CAPTCHA on 50+ Discord servers. San Francisco, United States, November 13th, 2026 – Solo , a privacy-preserving proof-of-humanity company, is bringing its human verification software development kit (SDK) to JellyJelly. The social video app runs on Solana and was co-founded by Venmo co-founder Iqram Magdon-Ismail. The integration lets JellyJelly confirm that every account belongs to a real, unique person, with no government ID and no puzzles to solve. Magdon-Ismail is co-founder and CEO of JellyJelly and an advisor to Solo. He co-developed the SDK behind the integration, shaping both its architecture and the way new users are onboarded. The move comes as AI agents learn to pass the tests meant to keep them out. In an experiment run by Solo, an AI agent named Gary joined more than 50 Discord servers overnight and sent over 500 messages. No one identified it as an AI agent. Gary had two instructions: pass every CAPTCHA challenge and accept the terms of service. It completed both through ordinary browsing and clicking, without any custom exploits. events.excerpt: Microsoft 365 services are slowly recovering from a prolonged outage that has handed critics of single-vendor dependence a particularly unwelcome case study. Ever wondered what it would be like if your IT supplier abruptly pulled the plug? Perhaps the result of a mood swing by an unpredictable political leader? For affected Microsoft customers, the disruption has offered an unwelcome preview. Email? Gone. Messaging with Teams? Iffy. Collaboration? Nope. The list of problems in what Microsoft delicately called a "Service Degradation" is breathtaking. The company put the incident's start at 1826 GMT on November 12. Exchange Online fell over. Viewing recently used files in the Microsoft 365 application was problematic. Copilot threw a wobbly. Microsoft 365 Education was affected (unfortunate, considering the changes the company has made ), and so on. At 1401 GMT on November 13, Microsoft reported: "We're continuing to see improvements in service availability," but the damage has surely been done. If the outage halted work at your organization, then questions will have to be asked. Even Microsoft's rivals had some sympathy for the engineers and administrators dealing with the problems. events.excerpt: Zeeder is the Zcash Foundation’s DNS seeder, the service that helps new Zcash nodes find their first peers. If you run your own seeder from our Docker image, this affects you. If you only run a node or a wallet, there is nothing to do. What changed The image was published as zfnd/dnsseeder , a name left over from the old Go seeder. It is now zfnd/zeeder : zfnd/zeeder - Docker Image Both names hold the same image today. Timeline Until 14 December 2026: every release goes to both names. From 14 December 2026: releases go to zfnd/zeeder only. Old zfnd/dnsseeder tags stay pullable, but latest is removed there. What to do Swap zfnd/dnsseeder for zfnd/zeeder in your Docker or Compose setup before 14 December. 1 post - 1 participant Read full topic
